advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-stamp each drift-floored finding with decision='dropped' before moving it into verdict['dropped'] so surfaced_findings excludes it from future prior sets (mirror code_review/workflow_ops.py:441).
evidence: drift_floor.py:251 `dropped.append({**f, "_floored": True, "novelty": nov, "drop_reason": "drift"})` — no `decision` re-stamp
sidecar.py:311 `SURFACED_DECISIONS = ("block", "advisory")` and sidecar.py:324 `if f.get("decision") in SURFACED_DECISIONS`
sidecar.py:429 `"decision": f.get("decision")` — build_payload persists the finding's own decision for the dropped bucket, no override

sidecar.py:302-310 comment: 'a finding permanently dropped for convergence re-enters the prior set and re-matches on recurrence, scoring LOW novelty ("carryover") and thereby ESCAPING the floor that dropped it'
code_review/workflow_ops.py:441 `f["decision"] = "dropped"` — the correct re-stamp pattern when moving a finding into the dropped bucket
drift_floor_drop keeps carryovers: decide.py:149-150 `if novelty < t_novel: return False`
advisory.finding: Drift-floored findings are moved into verdict['dropped'] without re-stamping decision='dropped'. build_payload persists them with their original decision ('block'/'advisory'), and sidecar.surfaced_findings filters on SURFACED_DECISIONS=('block','advisory') — so a drift-dropped finding re-enters the prior set on the next drift re-review, scores as carryover (low novelty), and drift_floor_drop keeps carryovers → the finding permanently re-blocks. This defeats the convergence goal and violates the 'old-frilly-plankton' re-entry invariant.
scenarios: A drift-dropped blocking finding is persisted decision='block'; the next drift re-review reads it as prior, scores it carryover, and drift_floor_drop keeps it → re-BLOCK, no convergence
advisory.suggested_fix: In apply_to_verdict, build the dropped record as `{**f, "decision": "dropped", "_floored": True, "novelty": nov, "drop_reason": "drift"}`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat an empty drifted-files set as 'no drift to converge' (skip the floor) or as unknown, so an empty git diff cannot drop every novel finding.
evidence: drift_floor.py:61 `return sorted({ln.strip() for ln in out.stdout.splitlines() if ln.strip()})` — empty stdout yields [] not None
drift_floor.py:150-151 drifted_files is computed only when code_drifted (SHAs differ), so [] passes through as an eligible drifted set
drift_floor.py:236-237 `if drifted_files is None: return` — only None short-circuits; [] proceeds
decide.py:151 `return not (set(cited_paths) & set(drifted_files))` — with an empty drifted set every novel finding is dropped
maybe_apply drift_floor.py:302-303 only guards `drifted_raw is None`, not empty
advisory.finding: When the signed SHA differs from HEAD but `git diff --name-only base..head` yields no files (empty commit, amended/same-tree commit, revert), _drifted_paths returns [] (not None). The candidate stays eligible with drifted_files=[], and apply_to_verdict only short-circuits on None — so an empty drift set intersects nothing and EVERY novel finding is dropped, converting a genuine BLOCK re-review into PASS. The None fail-safe is bypassed by the [] case.
scenarios: Signed at SHA A, HEAD is B, but B..A has no file changes (empty/amend/revert commit): all novel blocking findings dropped, BLOCK→PASS on a real re-review
advisory.suggested_fix: Short-circuit in maybe_apply/apply_to_verdict when `not drifted_files` (empty set), not only when it is None; or make _drifted_paths return None when the diff is empty despite differing SHAs.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add the `indeterminate and not surfaced → INDETERMINATE` branch to _recompute_verdict_after_drop so it matches finalize_verdict.
evidence: drift_floor.py:210-211 `else: verdict["verdict"] = "PASS"`
orchestrator.py:514-515 `elif indeterminate and not surfaced: verdict = "INDETERMINATE"` — the branch _recompute omits
docstring drift_floor.py:191 claims 'using the SAME rule as orchestrator.finalize_verdict'
advisory.finding: _recompute_verdict_after_drop diverges from orchestrator.finalize_verdict: in the non-llm_unavailable / non-verify_failed branch it unconditionally sets PASS, but finalize_verdict yields INDETERMINATE when `indeterminate and not surfaced`. If the drift floor empties `blocking` while indeterminate findings remain and no advisory survives, the true verdict is INDETERMINATE, not PASS.
scenarios: A drifted re-review with a novel blocking finding (dropped) plus indeterminate findings and no surviving advisory: finalize_verdict→INDETERMINATE, _recompute→PASS (potentially signs a hollow PASS)
advisory.suggested_fix: Before the final else, add: `elif (verdict.get('indeterminate') or []) and not (verdict.get('advisory') or []): verdict['verdict'] = 'INDETERMINATE'`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor drift_floor_candidate's code_drifted on the same authoritative SHA compute_validity uses for stale-head (_authoritative_head), or correct the docstring's 'mirrors exactly' claim.
evidence: drift_floor.py:124-126 `signed_sha = signing.verified_at_sha_from_manifest(manifest)` / `current_sha = signing.head_sha(...)`
attest.py:591-592 compute_validity uses `signed_head = _authoritative_head(attestation)` then `if head == "unknown" or signed_head != head:` for stale-head
attest.py:457-467 _authoritative_head returns op-cert `merged_log_commit` (signed), NOT the plaintext head_sha/manifest sha
drift_floor.py:123 comment claims it 'mirrors compute_validity's unscoped whole-HEAD stale-head trigger anchor exactly'
advisory.finding: drift_floor_candidate's code_drifted anchor (verified_at_sha_from_manifest vs signing.head_sha) is not the same anchor compute_validity uses for the unscoped stale-head trigger (_authoritative_head — the op-cert SIGNED merged_log_commit, per SECURITY finding B — vs HEAD). The docstring claims it 'mirrors compute_validity's unscoped whole-HEAD stale-head trigger anchor exactly', but for op-cert records the two SHAs can differ, so the floor can be eligible when no stale-head re-review actually fired (or vice versa).
scenarios: An op-cert plan-review where merged_log_commit differs from the manifest verified-at-sha: the drift floor's eligibility anchor disagrees with the actual stale-head trigger

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the truncated/garbled sentences in drift_floor.maybe_apply and apply_to_verdict docstrings.
evidence: drift_floor.py:291-294 'The whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER ... is untouched — this re-review OUTCOME. Self-gates inert ... when not eligible, the unknown, or there is no prior surfaced memory.'
drift_floor.py:230-231 'Dropping a BLOCKING finding can flip BLOCK→PASS, so string is re-derived.'
advisory.finding: Docstrings in maybe_apply and apply_to_verdict are garbled/truncated, leaving the contract unclear (e.g. 'is untouched — this re-review OUTCOME', 'Self-gates inert ... when not eligible, the unknown, or there is no prior surfaced memory', 'Dropping a BLOCKING finding can flip BLOCK→PASS, so string is re-derived').
scenarios: A future maintainer reads the truncated sentences and misreads the gating/OUTCOME contract

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add candidate tests driving `within_window=False` (stale timestamp) and `prior_sidecar=False` (no prior findings) → `eligible is False`.
evidence: drift_floor.py:143-148 computes `within_window` from `latest_review_timestamp` and `window_minutes`
drift_floor.py:138-141 computes `prior_sidecar` from sidecar findings text
Tests present: test_candidate_not_eligible_when_material_changed / _when_code_unchanged / _when_registry_changed / _without_signature — but no _when_stale_out_of_window and no _when_no_prior_sidecar
ABSENCE: `_patch_candidate` always sets `last_ts_offset_ns=0` and non-empty `prior_findings`, so both gates are always True in every candidate test
advisory.finding: The `within_window` and `prior_sidecar` eligibility preconditions of `drift_floor_candidate` have no negative-path test. Tests drive `signed`, `plan_unchanged`, `code_drifted`, and `registry_unchanged` to False individually, but never `within_window=False` (stale prior review beyond the freshness window) nor `prior_sidecar=False` (no prior findings). A regression that dropped or inverted either gate — e.g. flooring a re-review outside the freshness window, or with no prior surfaced memory — would not be caught.
scenarios: A drift re-review whose last sidecar is older than remediation_window_minutes
A drift re-review with an empty/whitespace prior findings set
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two tests using `_patch_candidate(monkeypatch, last_ts_offset_ns=<window+1 in ns>)` and `_patch_candidate(monkeypatch, prior_findings=())`, asserting the respective reason is False and `eligible is False`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add apply_to_verdict tests where the emptied-BLOCK verdict has `coverage['llm_unavailable']` (→ INDETERMINATE) and `coverage['verify_failed']` with/without a blocking indeterminate criterion (→ INDETERMINATE/PASS).
evidence: drift_floor.py:201-211 branches on `cov.get('llm_unavailable')` and `cov.get('verify_failed')` to produce INDETERMINATE vs PASS
test_apply_drift_floor_flips_to_pass_when_only_novel_noise (tests:125-134) exercises only the else→PASS branch; `_blocked_verdict` coverage has neither `llm_unavailable` nor `verify_failed`
ABSENCE: no test sets `coverage['llm_unavailable']`/`coverage['verify_failed']` before applying the floor
advisory.finding: `_recompute_verdict_after_drop`'s INDETERMINATE branches are untested. Only the plain BLOCK→PASS path (empty blocking, no coverage flags) is exercised; the `coverage['llm_unavailable']` → INDETERMINATE and `coverage['verify_failed']` → INDETERMINATE/PASS branches added by this diff have no test.
scenarios: A drift re-review that emptied the blocking bucket while coverage reports llm_unavailable or verify_failed
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend the flip-to-pass test into a table over coverage flags asserting the re-derived verdict string for each branch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a maybe_apply test with an eligible drift + known drift set but a prior sidecar whose findings are all non-surfaced (e.g. `decision='dropped'`), asserting the verdict is left byte-identical.
evidence: drift_floor.py:315 `prior_findings = sidecar.surfaced_findings(prior)` then 316 early-returns when empty
test_maybe_apply_floors_when_eligible (tests:282-308) patches `latest_review_result` to a surfaced advisory finding — the non-empty path only
ABSENCE: no maybe_apply test where `surfaced_findings(prior)` is empty (e.g. prior only has dropped/indeterminate findings) asserting the floor stays inert
advisory.finding: `maybe_apply`'s empty-input early return (`if not combined or not prior_findings: return` at drift_floor.py:316) is not covered. Tests cover not-eligible and unknown-drift-set inert paths, but never the eligible-with-drift-but-no-surfaced-prior case, so the surfaced-only prior gate (guarding against a previously-dropped finding re-entering as carryover) is untested at the entry seam.
scenarios: Eligible drift re-review whose only prior sidecar findings were previously dropped (non-surfaced)
advisory.suggested_fix: Patch `latest_review_result` to `{'findings':[{'id':'p','finding':'x','decision':'dropped'}]}` and assert `v['dropped']==[]` and verdict unchanged.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Treat a NOVEL finding with an empty `kind=='file'` citation set as KEEP (fail-safe), or extend the drift-intersection to symbol/name citations, so a novel finding about drifted code cannot be dropped merely for lacking a file-path citation.
evidence: drift_floor.py:183-187 `_finding_cited_paths` returns only `c['path'] for ... c.get('kind') == 'file' and c.get('path')` — symbol/name citations produce an empty set
decide.py:149-151 `if novelty < t_novel: return False` then `return not (set(cited_paths) & set(drifted_files))` → empty cited_paths ⇒ `not (∅) == True` ⇒ DROP
tests/unit/test_plan_review_drift_floor.py:44-46 asserts `drift_floor_drop(0.9, cited_paths=set(), ...) is True` — confirms a novel finding with NO file citations is DROPPED by design
findings.py:159 `if cit.get('kind') != 'file': continue` and grounding tests (`{'kind':'symbol','name':...}`) confirm symbol-kind citations exist and carry `name`, not `path`

plan-review-novelty.eval.yaml N4-novel: 'a rebase endpoint that HEAD renamed since the plan was signed, so the cited call no longer resolves' — a drift finding whose citation may be a renamed symbol, which yields no `path` and would be dropped rather than kept
advisory.finding: drift_floor_drop drops any NOVEL finding with an empty file-citation set (no `kind=='file'` citation), because `_finding_cited_paths` ignores `kind=='symbol'` / free-text citations, so `set() & drifted_files` is always empty → DROP. A genuinely novel BLOCKING finding about DRIFTED code that cites it only via a symbol/name citation (e.g. a renamed function/endpoint) is silently suppressed and can flip BLOCK→PASS — defeating the code-drift detection this module claims to preserve.
scenarios: A re-review after HEAD drift mints a novel BLOCKING security finding about a renamed/removed symbol in the drifted code, cited via `kind=='symbol'` (or free-text) rather than `kind=='file'`; the drift floor drops it and re-derives the verdict to PASS.
A novel blocking finding about drifted code whose file citation was downgraded to non-`file` by the grounding validator (unresolved path) loses its path and is dropped.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `drift_floor_drop` (or `apply_to_verdict`), when a novel finding's `cited_paths` is empty, KEEP it (fail-safe) rather than DROP; alternatively resolve symbol/name citations to files before intersecting with drifted_files.
